questions.question: Which of the following Sections of the Indian Penal Code deals with 'rape'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 375**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 375** of the Indian Penal Code defines the offense of rape.
 
• This section outlines the different circumstances under which a sexual act is considered rape, including lack of consent, consent obtained through force or fraud, and situations involving minors.
 
• It specifies the punishment for rape, which can vary depending on the severity of the crime.
 
• The section has been amended several times to address changing societal norms and to strengthen the legal framework for protecting victims of sexual violence.
 
• Section 375 is a crucial part of India's legal system aimed at safeguarding the dignity and bodily autonomy of individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** was enacted in 1860 and is the principal criminal code of India.
 
• It covers all substantive aspects of criminal law and has been amended numerous times to keep pace with the changing needs of society.
 
• Other important sections related to sexual offenses include **Section 376** (punishment for rape) and **Section 354** (assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty).
 
• The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, also known as the Nirbhaya Act, brought significant changes to the IPC, including stricter punishments for sexual offenses.
 
• The IPC is complemented by other laws such as the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenses (POCSO) Act, which specifically addresses sexual crimes against minors.

questions.question: What is a revenue deficit in the government budget?

options.text: The excess of expenditure over revenue, excluding interest payments on debt
The excess of revenue over expenditure, excluding interest payments on debt
The excess of revenue over expenditure, including interest payments on debt
The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The excess of expenditure over revenue, including interest payments on debt** is known as a revenue deficit in the government budget.
 
• A revenue deficit indicates that the government's revenue receipts are not sufficient to meet its revenue expenditure.
 
• This type of deficit is a key indicator of the financial health of the government and reflects its ability to manage its finances.
 
• A persistent revenue deficit can lead to higher borrowings and increased debt burden for the government.
 
• Reducing the revenue deficit is crucial for maintaining fiscal discipline and ensuring long-term economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue receipts** include tax revenues (like income tax, corporate tax, GST) and non-tax revenues (like interest receipts, dividends, and profits from public sector enterprises).
 
• **Revenue expenditure** includes expenses incurred for the normal functioning of government departments and various services, interest payments on debt, and subsidies.
 
• Unlike capital expenditure, revenue expenditure does not result in the creation of assets or reduction in liabilities.
 
• Efforts to reduce revenue deficit may include enhancing revenue receipts through better tax compliance and administration, and rationalizing expenditure.
 
• The government may also implement structural reforms to improve the efficiency and productivity of public sector enterprises.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India vests plenary powers in Parliament to legislate on the subject of citizenship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 11**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 11** of the Constitution of India vests plenary powers in Parliament to legislate on the subject of citizenship.
 
• This article gives Parliament the authority to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
 
• It is part of Part II of the Constitution, which deals with the citizenship of individuals at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Article 11 empowers the Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
 
• This provision ensures that the Parliament has the flexibility to address all issues related to citizenship as and when required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5 to 11) deals with the citizenship of individuals at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Article 11 gives the Parliament the power to regulate the right of citizenship by law, which allows for necessary amendments and changes to adapt to evolving circumstances.

questions.question: What is the name of the famous British social reformer known for founding the Indian Home Rule League in 1916?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annie Besant** was a prominent British social reformer, theosophist, and supporter of Indian self-rule.
 
• She founded the **Indian Home Rule League** in 1916 to promote self-governance and greater autonomy for India within the British Empire.
 
• Annie Besant was also known for her work in education and women's rights, and she played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Her efforts helped to galvanize support for the cause of Indian self-rule and set the stage for future leaders like Mahatma Gandhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annie Besant** was born on 1st October 1847 in London and became involved in various social and political causes throughout her life.
 
• She became the president of the **Theosophical Society** and moved to India, where she became deeply involved in Indian politics.
 
• The **Indian Home Rule League** aimed to achieve self-government for India through constitutional means and fostered a sense of national unity.
 
• In recognition of her contributions, she was elected as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
 
• Her legacy continues to be remembered in India for her contributions to social reform, education, and the independence movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is a rare group of genetic disorders caused by mutations of certain genes affecting the colour (pigmentation) of the skin, hair and eyes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Albinism**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albinism** is a rare group of genetic disorders caused by mutations of certain genes affecting the color (pigmentation) of the skin, hair, and eyes.
 
• People with albinism are at risk of skin and vision problems due to the lack of melanin, the pigment responsible for coloration.
 
• Albinism can occur in all racial and ethnic groups.
 
• There is no cure for albinism, but individuals can manage symptoms with proper skin care and eye protection.
 
• Genetic counseling is recommended for families affected by albinism to understand the inheritance patterns and risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oculocutaneous albinism (OCA)** is the most common form, affecting the skin, hair, and eyes.
 
• **Ocular albinism** primarily affects the eyes, with minimal or no impact on skin and hair color.
 
• Individuals with albinism should avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen to protect their skin.
 
• Regular eye check-ups and visual aids can help manage vision issues associated with albinism.
 
• Public awareness and education are crucial to reduce the stigma and discrimination faced by individuals with albinism.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT with respect to High Yielding Varieties (HYVs)?

options.text: HYVs led to decrease in the cropping intensity.
HYVs had a shorter period of maturity.
They made green revolution technology as land-saving technology.
The usage of HYVs was complemented with the attraction of more investment in farm machines.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HYVs led to decrease in the cropping intensity**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** is incorrect as High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) led to an increase, not a decrease, in cropping intensity due to their shorter maturity period and higher productivity.
 
• **Option 2** is correct because HYVs indeed had a shorter period of maturity, allowing for multiple cropping cycles in a year.
 
• **Option 3** is correct as HYVs made green revolution technology a land-saving technology by increasing yield per hectare.
 
• **Option 4** is correct because the usage of HYVs was complemented with the attraction of more investment in farm machines, irrigation, and other inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The introduction of HYVs was a major component of the Green Revolution in India during the 1960s and 70s.
 
• HYVs required higher inputs of fertilizers, pesticides, and water, which led to an increase in agricultural productivity and self-sufficiency in food grains.
 
• The Green Revolution had significant socio-economic impacts, including changes in agricultural practices, rural incomes, and labor dynamics.
 
• Despite the benefits, the Green Revolution also brought about challenges such as environmental degradation, inequity among farmers, and over-reliance on chemical inputs.

questions.question: Who was the Indian Buddhist monk who is credited with the development of many ancient martial art forms in the 5th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bodhidharma**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bodhidharma** was an Indian Buddhist monk who is traditionally credited with transmitting Chan Buddhism to China.
 
• He is also considered the founder of the Shaolin Monastery and is associated with the development of many ancient martial art forms in the 5th century.
 
• Bodhidharma's teachings and practice centered on meditation and the Lankavatara Sutra, which emphasizes the realization of Buddha-nature.
 
• His contributions have had a lasting impact on both Buddhist practice and martial arts in East Asia.

• **Paramartha** was an Indian Buddhist missionary who translated texts and propagated Buddhism in China.
 
• **Atisa** was a Buddhist teacher from the Pala Empire in India who helped establish the Sarma schools of Tibetan Buddhism.
 
• The Shaolin Monastery, linked to Bodhidharma, is renowned for its association with Chinese martial arts and Chan (Zen) Buddhism.
 
• Legends suggest that Bodhidharma also developed exercises that later evolved into Shaolin Kung Fu, emphasizing physical fitness and self-defense.

questions.question: For which of the following discoveries in 1827 was the German physicist, Georg Simon Ohm best known?

options.text: For invention of the magnetometer, which is a device capable of measuring the direction and strength of a magnetic field
For developing a device capable of amplifying and modulating electromagnetic signals that could also function as an oscillator
For measuring the magnetic properties of nuclear particles
For clarifying the mathematical relationship between electrical current, resistance and voltage

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For clarifying the mathematical relationship between electrical current, resistance and voltage**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Georg Simon Ohm** was a German physicist and mathematician.
 
• He is best known for **Ohm's Law**, which states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• This law is usually expressed with the formula **V = IR**, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• Ohm's work was crucial in the field of electrical engineering and physics, providing a fundamental principle for understanding electrical circuits.
 
• His discovery in 1827 significantly contributed to the development of electrical theory and technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ohm's work initially received little recognition, but it later earned him significant honors, including the **Copley Medal** from the Royal Society of London.
 
• He also made contributions to the understanding of acoustics and the measurement of electrical resistance.
 
• Ohm's Law remains a fundamental concept in the study and application of electrical circuits today.
 
• His discoveries laid the groundwork for future innovations in electrical engineering and technology.

__
 
• **Tehri Hydroelectric Power Plant** is the tallest hydroelectric power plant in India as of 2022.
 
• Located in the state of Uttarakhand, the Tehri Dam is a multi-purpose rock and earth-fill embankment dam on the Bhagirathi River.
 
• The dam is 260.5 meters (855 ft) high, making it the highest dam in India and one of the tallest in the world.
 
• It plays a crucial role in water supply, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation, with an installed capacity of 1,000 MW.
 
• The project is managed by the Tehri Hydro Development Corporation Limited (THDC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Tehri Dam was constructed over a period of nearly 30 years, with the construction starting in 1978 and the dam becoming operational in 2006.
 
• The dam's reservoir, Tehri Lake, is a major tourist attraction and provides water for drinking and irrigation purposes to a large population.
 
• The Tehri Dam is also designed to withstand seismic activities, given its location in a seismically active region.
 
• It is a vital part of India's efforts to harness renewable energy and reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• The project faced several challenges, including environmental concerns and displacement of local communities, which were addressed through various mitigation measures.

questions.question: The __________ results from an increase in the proportion of workers relative to nonworkers in the population.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**demographic dividend**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **demographic dividend** refers to the economic growth potential that can result from shifts in a population’s age structure.
 
• This shift occurs when the proportion of the working-age population (15-64 years) is larger compared to the non-working-age population (below 15 and above 64 years).
 
• During this period, the workforce grows more rapidly than the dependent population, providing a window of opportunity for economic growth.
 
• To harness the demographic dividend, it is crucial to invest in health, education, and employment opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of the demographic dividend is closely linked to the demographic transition theory, which describes the transition from high birth and death rates to lower birth and death rates as a country develops.
 
• Countries in different stages of this transition can experience varying economic impacts based on their demographic profiles.
 
• Effective policy measures and investments in human capital are essential to convert the demographic potential into actual economic benefits.

questions.question: From which of the following states was Vibrant Village programme launched, on 10 April 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Vibrant Village programme was launched from **Arunachal Pradesh** on 10 April 2023.
 
• The programme aims to enhance the quality of life for people living in border villages, ensuring sustainable development and improving infrastructure.
 
• It focuses on areas such as education, health, agriculture, and connectivity to ensure comprehensive growth.
 
• Special emphasis is placed on empowering local communities and promoting tourism to generate livelihood opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** is known for its unique cultural heritage and scenic beauty, making it a crucial region for such developmental programmes.
 
• The Vibrant Village programme is a part of the government's broader strategy to bolster border security and enhance the living standards of border communities.
 
• By improving the infrastructure in these remote areas, the programme also aims to curb migration to urban areas, thereby maintaining the demographic stability of border regions.
